answer: Payouts leave through a wharf where every load needs a manifest, and manifest capacity follows the holder's verified provenance rather than the capital behind it. Each unit of work carries a violet tag, invisible in normal use but readable under audit light, so relabeling a load as independent work is caught and the whole manifest voided. Burning ember is charged per reroute, and the k-th reroute an operator makes costs k squared, so shuffling n heads through one wharf burns n cubed over three. A manifest cannot be leased, and a wharf that accepts a voided one is slashed alongside its holder.
